title: 1983 AHSME Problem 23
statement: In the adjoining figure the five circles are tangent to one another consecutively and to the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2.\) If the radius of the largest circle is \(18\) and that of the smallest one is \(8,\) then the radius of the middle circle is

solutions.text:
The centers lie on the angle bisector of \(L_1\) and \(L_2.\) Similarity of the configuration for any two consecutive circles shows that consecutive radii have a constant ratio. Thus the five radii form a geometric sequence. If the middle radius is \(m,\) symmetry of a five-term geometric sequence gives \(m^2=8\cdot18,\) so \(m=12.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Every pair of consecutive tangent circles has the same shape after scaling
